books.section: Topic 8.2 The Cold War from 1945 to 1980
Truman and the Beginning of the Cold War (1945-1953)

stimulus.source_note: Original secondary passage written for this question; facts from the grounding books.
stimulus.text: Original secondary passage: The United States came out of World War II as the world's strongest power, while Europe's great powers lay in ruins. American leaders believed the peace had failed after World War I because nations had acted alone. This time they built a different order: a new United Nations to settle disputes together, American aid to rebuild friendly nations, and lasting alliances to deter aggression.

source: original; stimulus is an original secondary passage written for this question; facts from the grounding books
stem: According to the passage, why did American leaders build a United Nations after World War II?

options.text: To give the Soviet Union a veto over all American foreign policy.
options.misconception: The UN was a forum for settling disputes, not a veto over American foreign policy.

options.text: To settle disputes together, instead of nations acting alone as after World War I.
To replace the American army with an international police force.
options.misconception: The United States kept its own army after the war; the UN never replaced it.

options.text: To punish Germany and Japan by keeping them out of world affairs forever.
options.misconception: America rebuilt Germany and Japan as allies; it did not shut them out of world affairs forever.

rationales.A: The United Nations gave no country a veto over all American policy. The United States kept its own foreign policy and its own armed forces.
rationales.B: The passage says American leaders built the United Nations to settle disputes together, learning from the failure of nations acting alone after World War I. Background from the books: collective security, with America inside the system, was the new approach.
rationales.C: The United Nations never replaced the American army. The United States kept large armed forces and built alliances such as NATO.
rationales.D: The passage says nothing about punishing Germany and Japan forever. American policy rebuilt West Germany and Japan as allies instead.
rationales.general:
1. Read the lesson American leaders took. After World War I, nations acted alone and the peace failed.
2. Ask what the United Nations was for. The passage says it was built to settle disputes together.
3. Ask what 'together' means here. Background from the books: American policy now stressed collective security, with the United States inside the system instead of outside it.
4. Name the change. The United States stopped standing apart from world bodies and took a leading place in one.
Remember: the United Nations was America's answer to the failure of going it alone.
